name: IYKYK
blurb: If you know, you know: marks an inside joke only some people will get
title: IYKYK Meaning: What Does IYKYK Mean in Texts and Posts?
description: IYKYK stands for "if you know, you know": it marks an inside joke or reference only some readers will get. Origin, examples and when to skip it.
answer: IYKYK stands for "if you know, you know". People add it to a post or message to signal an inside joke, shared memory or niche reference that only certain readers will understand, without explaining it. Those who get it feel included; those who don't are meant to stay curious. The abbreviation has been used online since at least 2009 and became common in the mid-2010s.

body: The phrase "if you know, you know" is older spoken English. Dictionary.com finds the abbreviation on social media from at least 2009, with use growing in the mid-2010s, and it is now a familiar hashtag. Cambridge describes it as a way to show there is shared knowledge with the reader that other people might not understand.

ul: "That one teacher who said 'I'll wait.' IYKYK."
"Best tacos in the city are behind the gas station, iykyk."
"90s kids and the dial-up sound. IYKYK."

body: IYKYK is friendly and a bit mysterious. Used to tease an inside joke among friends it is fun; used by brands and influencers to hype a product, it can feel like gatekeeping or marketing. If people keep asking what you mean, just explain.

faq.q: How do you reply to IYKYK?
faq.a: If you get it, react or add to the joke. If you don't, it is fine to ask; people often enjoy explaining.
Not really, but it deliberately leaves some readers out, so overusing it can seem exclusive.
